questions.q: What are the three real migration paths from ADF to Fabric Data Factory?
options: Mounting ADF as a Fabric item, the built-in upgrade experience, and manual migration
Only manual migration — there's no automated option at all
Deleting the ADF and starting from scratch is the only path
Migration happens automatically with zero user action required
questions.explain: Microsoft offers three genuinely distinct paths, letting you choose based on pipeline complexity: mounting as a native item, an assessment-first upgrade tool, or full manual rebuild.

questions.q: Why is mounting an existing ADF into a Fabric workspace often a reasonable first step?
options: It gives visibility and side-by-side testing with zero pipeline rework
It permanently deletes the original ADF resource
It's the only path that supports SSIS packages
It automatically rewrites every pipeline into Fabric-native format
questions.explain: Mounting an ADF as a native Fabric item lets you view and manage it alongside Fabric artifacts without any rework — pipelines still execute in Azure, but you get visibility for planning.

questions.q: What happens to an ADF dataset's file path and format settings when migrating to Fabric?
options: They move inline, directly into the activity that used them (like the Copy activity's Source tab)
They're deleted and must be re-entered from scratch with no equivalent
They remain a separate object in Fabric, unchanged
They're automatically converted into a Dataflow Gen2
questions.explain: Because Fabric has no separate dataset object, the same file path and format information becomes inline configuration on whichever activity referenced that dataset.

questions.q: Which ADF capability has no direct Fabric equivalent and is genuinely still "to be determined" as of this course?
options: Azure-SSIS integration runtime
The Copy activity
If Condition and ForEach activities
The expression language
questions.explain: If your pipelines run real SSIS packages, that capability doesn't yet have a determined Fabric path, so plan to keep those pipelines on classic ADF for now.

questions.q: How does trigger/schedule management differ in Fabric compared to ADF during migration planning?
options: Fabric currently manages schedules per-pipeline, without ADF's centralized, reusable trigger model
Triggers work identically in both, with no migration considerations
Fabric doesn't support any form of scheduling
ADF's centralized triggers transfer automatically with no rebuild needed
questions.explain: Rebuilding triggers is a real step in the migration sequence, since Fabric's per-pipeline schedule model differs from ADF's centralized, reusable trigger approach.
